header.p: How to use Bid Board: score opportunities, get a Bid or No Bid recommendation, and complete CSO review.

li.a: CSO: Approve, decline, or request changes

main.p: Bid Board helps your organisation decide whether to pursue a tender or opportunity. You capture each opportunity as a project, answer a structured scorecard, and the app suggests Bid or No Bid based on the overall score (by default, 70% or above suggests Bid). A senior approver (CSO) then reviews and confirms the outcome. You can set a pipeline stage on each project, get deadline reminders, and see history of submissions.
Your administrator assigns one of these access levels in Odoo:

ul.li: Bid Board User — you create and work on projects you are involved in (see “Who can see which projects” below).
Bid Board Reviewer — same as a user, plus you can open any project and related items, which is needed for the review queue and oversight.
Bid Board Manager — same as a reviewer, plus access to Configuration (settings, email schedule, team list).

main.p: Who can click Approve, Decline, or Request change? That is controlled by email, not only by your access level. Your login email must be listed under Bid Board → Configuration → Settings → CSO (Email Approvers). If your email is not on that list, you will not see those buttons—even if you are a Reviewer or Manager. If you need to approve reviews, ask a manager to add your email there.

If you are on the CSO email list, you will not see Save draft or Submit for review on the project (those are for the bid team). You will see Approve, Decline, and Request change when the project is waiting for review or has changes requested.
Under the Bid Board app, the main entries are:

ul.li: Leads — CRM leads and opportunities (intake before an enquiry exists).
New Enquiry — quick start: name, client, lead, team, deadline, and progress.
Bid / No Bid — opens the decision-focused list (default filters and workflow context). Sub-menus: All Records (complete list of enquiries); Submissions (submit-for-review history).
Review & reminders — Review Queue (projects Pending review or Change requested, for approvers) and Deadline Reminders (reminder records for submission-deadline emails).
Reports → Project Reports — charts and tables to analyse projects (for reviewers/managers).
Analytics — one unified Bid Board Analytics screen with tabs: Leads, Enquiries, By sales rep, Proposals, and Activity & reminders.
Configuration → Settings — who gets emails, CSO list, and related options (managers).
Configuration → Email Schedule — when automated reminder jobs run (managers).
Configuration → Team — people you can tag on projects (name, department, role, email).
Documentation — this help page (last item in the bar).

main.p: This is the end-to-end path for one opportunity: where it starts, how it moves through review, how the enquiry ends, and (when you pursue the tender) how proposals close the commercial loop.
Work always converges on an enquiry (a Bid Board project). Typical starting points:

ul.li: Bid Board → Leads — intake in CRM; use your configured server actions to create a linked enquiry when ready.
New Enquiry / Bid / No Bid → All Records → New — create the enquiry directly.
Bid / No Bid or Bid / No Bid → All Records — open an existing record (parent menu uses decision-focused defaults; All Records lists every enquiry).

main.p: First to complete: Project info (client, value, duration, scope-of-work % ≤ 100%, deadlines, team) and the Scorecard (overall score drives the Bid / No bid recommendation; default rule uses 70% as the Bid threshold).

ol.li: Bid team: Submit for review → Pending review. Each submit is logged under Bid / No Bid → Submissions.
CSO (email on Configuration → Settings → CSO approvers): Approve, Decline, or Request change. Use Review & reminders → Review Queue if you have access.
If Request change: team edits, then Submit for review again.

main.p: If your organisation enabled a submit threshold, submission may be blocked until the overall score reaches the minimum.

ul.li: Approved + Bid — review is Approved; final decision Bid; Bid status stays Open until you mark Won, Lost, or Closed. You may create proposals next.
Approved + No bid — approved with No bid; Bid status is set to Closed. No proposal path.
Review declined — CSO Declined the submission; record is locked for typical users per your access rules.
No submission — enquiry stays in Draft or is left inactive (operational choice).

main.p: When the enquiry is Approved with Bid, open it from Bid / No Bid and use Create proposal. Defaults (including Scope of work from enquiry) flow from the enquiry.
End of proposal workflow: set outcome to Won or Lost on the proposal. The enquiry remains the permanent Bid / No bid record.
main.pre: START → Lead / New enquiry / Open enquiry ↓ Project info + Scorecard ↓ Submit for review → Pending review ↓ ┌─────┴─────┬──────────────┐ ↓ ↓ ↓ Decline Request change Approve ↓ ↓ ↓ END edit & re-submit final decision Bid or No bid ↓ ↓ loop No bid → END (enquiry declined) Bid → Create proposal → Open → Won/Lost → END
main.p: Each project has a stage such as New, Qualified, Proposition, or Won. Stages describe where the opportunity sits in your sales process. Stage is separate from review status (draft vs pending CSO, etc.).

ul.li: Active — work in progress.
Completed — CSO approved and the final decision was to Bid.
Declined — CSO declined the review, or the final decision was No bid after approval.
Priority — mark important deals; you can set this when creating or editing a project.
Draft — the team is still editing; use Save draft if you want to record that explicitly.
Pending review — submitted to CSO; waiting for Approve, Decline, or Request change.
Change requested — CSO asked for updates; adjust the project and submit again.
Approved — CSO signed off; the project may be read-only for the team until a CSO edits it.
Declined (review) — CSO rejected the submission; the record is locked like an approved one (only CSO, Bid Board managers, or administrators can change or delete it).
The app sets Bid when the overall score is at least 70%, otherwise No bid. That final decision drives the wording on the sheet and what happens after approval.

ol.li: Create a project — use New Project or copy an existing one. The app assigns a reference code such as BID-#####.
Project info tab — fill client, location (emirate), industry, contract details, bonds, KPI, scope percentages (they must add up to at most 100%), deadlines, team, and notes.

Scorecard tab — lines are added automatically for new enquiries (defaults start at the top score so you can submit once content is right; lower any row to reflect risk). Pick 1, 2, or 3 per line and weights; add short comments if helpful.
Decision sheet tab — check category scores, overall score, and the Bid / No bid recommendation from the score rule.
Submit for review — sends the project to CSO. A line appears in Bid / No Bid → Submissions. CSO may get an email depending on your company settings (see below).
CSO chooses Approve, Decline, or Request change (with comments and priority). Approving notifies commercial/bid contacts and optionally the person who created the project.
After approval — status becomes Completed if the final decision is Bid, or Declined if it is No bid. Any open change requests are closed.
If CSO requests changes, you get an email, update the project, and click Submit for review again.

main.p: On each project you can use the log at the bottom to leave messages and schedule activities like any other Odoo record.

ul.li: Save draft and Submit for review — for bid team members (not CSO approvers).
Approve, Decline, Request change — for CSO approvers (email on the CSO list, with reviewer/manager access).
The status bar shows where the review is: Draft → Pending review → Change requested → Approved or Declined.

main.p: Everything about the deal: title, reference code, client, sales rep, project lead, team tags, emirate, industry, contract length and value, type, risk threshold, tender and performance bonds, KPI, deadlines, progress, high-level status, and pipeline stage.
Split the work mix across cleaning, maintenance, security, landscaping, laundry, support, and other. The total must stay at or below 100%.

Criteria are grouped under Strategy, Customer, Commercial, Finance, and Operations. Each row has three wording options (columns 1–3); you pick the level 1, 2, or 3 that best matches the opportunity and set a weight if some factors matter more.
The app turns that into category scores and one overall score. New and duplicated enquiries get a standard set of scorecard rows automatically; you can edit them as needed.
Here you see the five category scores (read-only), the overall score, short recommendation text, the Bid / No bid outcome from the score rule, and review status.
main.h2: CSO: Approve, decline, or request changes

ul.li: Approve — closes the review as approved, records who approved and when, sets project status to Completed (Bid) or Declined (No bid), closes open change requests, and sends notification emails per settings.
Decline — marks the review declined and the project declined; notifies lead, creator, and managers as configured.
Request change — opens a short form for priority and comments; the project goes to Change requested and the creator gets an email with your notes.

main.p: After Approval, team members who are not on the CSO email list usually cannot edit or delete the project; CSO approvers still can if something must be corrected.
Each time someone clicks Submit for review, a submission line is created with the date and owner. View the list under Bid / No Bid → Submissions or on the project’s Submissions tab.
When CSO asks for changes, those requests appear on the project with priority and comments. They are marked resolved when the review is completed.

The system can send emails 7 days, 3 days, and 1 day before the submission deadline to the project lead and, where set, selected team members. Approved or declined projects stop receiving these reminders. Details of sent reminders may appear on the reminder record and in the project log.

ul.li: Submit for review — to CSO addresses when “notify on every submission” is on, or when the score is above 80% if that option is off (exact behaviour is set in Settings).
Approval — to commercial and bid managers, and optionally the person who created the project.
Decline — to project lead, creator, and managers as configured.
Change requested — to the project creator.
Test email — from Settings, to check that notifications look correct.

main.p: Bid Board needs a valid “from” address in Settings or in your organisation’s general outgoing mail settings in Odoo. If sending fails, a note may appear on the project’s log explaining why.

p.strong: Automated daily checks (managers can see timing under Email schedule)

ul.li: Governance reminder — reminds CSO if a project has waited too long for review (based on Pending review SLA days in Settings) or if a follow-up activity is due soon.
Deadline reminders — sends the T-7 / T-3 / T-1 emails described above.

main.p: Open Bid Board → Configuration → Settings. There should be only one settings record—edit it, do not create extra copies.

ul.li: Notification from — the sender name and address on Bid Board emails.
CSO (Email approvers) — who may use Approve / Decline / Request change (comma-separated emails).
Notify CSO on every submission — if turned off, CSO is emailed mainly when the score is high (above 80%).

Submit threshold — open Bid Board → Configuration → Submit Threshold and set a percentage (key: sales_bid_board.submit_review_min_score). Users can submit for review only when overall score is at or above this value.
Commercial manager email and Bid manager email — who gets approval/decline notifications (you can list several addresses separated by commas).
Notify creator on approval — optional copy to whoever created the project.
Pending review SLA days — how many days’ wait triggers a governance reminder to CSO.
Test recipient and Send test email — check that mail works before go-live.

main.p: Users normally see projects they created, lead, sell, or are on as a linked team member (with an Odoo user on that team entry).
Reviewers and managers can open all projects and related submissions, reminders, and change requests—needed for oversight and the review queue.
Managers also maintain settings, the team directory, and can review the email schedule.
Project reports lets you build pivot tables, charts, and lists of projects—filter by status, review stage, group by pipeline stage or lead, and so on.

Bid Board Analytics is a single tabbed dashboard for leadership. Each tab supports filters and drill-down to lists/forms from KPIs, charts, and table rows: Leads, Enquiries, By sales rep, Proposals, and Activity & reminders.
Proposals also show Scope of work (from enquiry), which flows from the linked Bid / No Bid enquiry so commercial users always see the same scope split.
